'''Emma Naluyima''' (born circa 1980) is a Ugandan [[veterinarian]], [[farmer|urban farmer]], businesswoman, elementary school educator and animal & crop farming instructor.<ref name="1R">{{cite web|newspaper=[[Daily Monitor]] | url=https://www.monitor.co.ug/Magazines/Farming/After-sharing-her-story--Naluyima-now-sells-40-more-piglets-/689860-1996376-j4s9cm/index.html |title=After sharing her story, Naluyima now sells 40 more Camborough piglets each month |date=18 September 2013 | author=Esther Oluka |access-date=19 August 2020 | location=Kampala}}</ref><ref name="2R">{{cite web| url=https://observer.ug/lifestyle/66116-at-40-dr-emma-naluyima-s-triumphs-are-enviable |title=At 40, Dr Emma Naluyima's triumphs are enviable |newspaper=[[The Observer (Uganda)]] |date=14 August 2020 |author=Carolyne Nakazibwe |access-date=19 August 2020 | place=Kampala}}</ref> It is calculated that she earns approximately US$100,000 annually from her farm situated on {{convert|1.0|acre|ha}}, in Bwerenga, [[Wakiso District]], Uganda.<ref name="3R">{{cite web|newspaper=[[Daily Monitor]] | url=https://www.monitor.co.ug/Magazines/Farming/Dr--Emma-Naluyima--Baba-Dioum-win-US-100-000/689860-5260790-y0whjk/index.html |title=Uganda and Baba Dioum of Senegal jointly win US$100,000 Africa Food Prize at the African Green Revolution Forum |date=4 September 2019 |access-date=19 August 2020 | author=Daily Monitor |place=Kampala}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Naluyima was born circa 1980 in [[Entebbe]], Uganda. Her father, Chris Kikwabanga, was an airline pilot and her mother, Margaret Nanziri, was a banker.<ref name="2R"/> Naluyima attended Stella Maris Primary School in [[Nkokonjeru]], in [[Buikwe District]]. For her O-Level and A-Level studies, she attended [[Maryhill High School]] in the city of [[Mbarara]]. She was then admitted to [[Makerere University]], Uganda's largest and oldest [[public university]], graduating with a [[Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine]] degree. Later, she was awarded a [[Master of Science|Master of Health Services Research]] in Veterinary Medicine, by Makerere University.<ref name="2R"/>

==Career==
When Naluyima graduated with her BVM degree in 2004, the ''National Animal Genetic Resources Centre and Databank'' (''Nagric''), in Entebbe, offered her a full-time job, complete with a government house. After two years at Nagric, she resigned from the salaried job, in August 2006 and started her first piggery, on a small family plot of land, with USh2 million (approximately US$1,000 at that time) of borrowed money. That piggery paid for her master's degree. In 2010, she married Ssalongo Washington Mugerwa, a school teacher. They bought {{convert|6.5|acre|0}} and Naluyima relocated her ten pigs to their new home.<ref name="2R"/>

==Investments==
[[File:Dr Naluyima's students.jpg|thumb|220x220px|Dr Naluyima's Students]]
Her current portfolio includes
(a) a plantation of [[matooke]] and vegetables, including [[tomato]]es, [[spinach]], [[cucumber]], [[potato]]es and greens.<ref name="2R" /> (b) A piggery of approximately 30 ''Camborough pigs''.<ref name="4R">{{cite web |newspaper=[[Daily Monitor]] | url=https://www.monitor.co.ug/Magazines/Farming/Camborough-Pigs--A-breed-that-is-worth-the-cost/689860-1613278-15lwmqaz/index.html |title=Camborough Pigs: A breed that is worth the cost |date=7 November 2012 |author=Nelson Muhanguzi |access-date=19 August 2020 |place=Kampala}}</ref> (c) Entebbe Animal Care Centre, a veterinary clinic.<ref name="4R" /> (d) An elementary school with approximately 300 students and 20 teachers.<ref name="2R" />

(e) A snail farm where snail glue is sold to cosmetic manufacturers.<ref name="2R" /> (f) She also keeps about one dozen dairy cows, a flock of chickens and four above-ground plastic fishponds stocked with [[tilapia]] and [[catfish]].<ref name="5R">{{cite web| url=https://news.ilri.org/2018/03/07/ugandan-emma-naluyima-describes-her-thriving-pigcrop-farm-at-the-global-forum-for-food-and-agriculture/ |title=Ugandan Emma Naluyima describes her thriving pig+crop farm at the Global Forum for Food and Agriculture |publisher=[[International Livestock Research Institute]] |date=7 March 2018 |author=Susan McMillan | 
access-date=19 August 2020 |place=Nairobi}}</ref> (g) Tours of her farm cost USh100,000 (approx. US$28) per head.<ref name="2R" /> She calls her farm '''One Acre Limited'''.<ref name="5R" />

==Awards==
In September 2019, Emma Naluyima was a joint winner of the 2019 [[Africa Food Prize]] (formerly the Yara Prize). Her joint winner was [[Baba Dioum]] of [[Senegal]]. The two shared a US$100,000 cash prize.<ref name="3R"/>

==Family==
Emma Naluyima is married to Ssalongo Washington Mugerwa with whom she has four children, including a set of twin-firstborn daughters, born circa 2011.<ref name="2R"/>
